positions.title: Analyse génotype-phénotype à grande échelle chez les poissons
positions.host_institution: Institut de Biologie de l'École Normale Supérieure
positions.research_field: Les téléostéens ont de plus subi une duplication complète du génome (WGD) à l'origine de leur radiation, suivie d'événements supplémentaires chez les Salmoniformes et les Cypriniformes. Cette complexité génomique, avec 20–30 % de gènes dupliqués retenus dans les espèces actuelles, complique l'inférence des relations d'orthologie mais élargit également la cible mutationnelle pour l'innovation fonctionnelle convergente. De riches bases de données phénotypiques complètent les ressources génomiques en documentant des milliers de traits écologiques, morphologiques et physiologiques : FishBase, l'Encyclopedia of Life (données FishShapes) et Phenoscape rendent les études de corrélation génotype-phénotype systématiques hautement faisables chez les poissons.

positions.title: Identification des signatures neuronales des capacités cognitives infracliniques à la phase aigue du coma (UNLOCK)
positions.host_institution: ToNIC-Toulouse NeuroImaging Center (UMR 1214)
positions.research_field:
The UNLOCK project has a direct relation with the BEST research axis “Understanding and promoting healthy living and well-being” by addressing a major unmet need in patients with DoC: the ability to accurately detect preserved cognition, predict recovery and restore meaningful interaction with their environment. By developing affordable bedside neurotechnologies for continuous, longitudinal multimodal assessments, UNLOCK will deepen our understanding of how consciousness and cognition re-emerge after severe brain injury. Its innovative investigation of brain-body interactions, will also reveal how bodily states influence information processing during the acute phase of coma. 
UNLOCK also contributes to the promoting of well-being through a genuinely patient-centred and personalized approach. By integrating multimodal physiological and neural signals with machine learning and AI-empowered-BCIs, the project aims to identify covert consciousness, anticipate individual treatment responses and support personalized therapeutic stimulation. Ultimately, restoring even basic communication between patients, caregivers and families could reduce the profound isolation experienced by individuals who remain conscious but behaviorally unresponsive. UNLOCK therefore connects fundamental neuroscience research with tangible improvements in care, autonomy, cognitive engagement and quality of life for patients and their families 
Built upon highly disruptive technologies, the nature of the current project is not incremental and represents a paradigm shift in our understanding of consciousness, opening the door to major breakthroughs in neuroscience, neurotechnology, and rehabilitative medicine. By tackling these ambitious goals, UNLOCK has the potential to reshape the landscape of brain injured patient care, from the acute to the chronic DoC phases. UNLOCK will represent a very valuable strategic asset for our country for the years to come, therefore guaranteeing a French leadership in this major topic of medical research.

positions.title: PULSE-MASLD : Rôle des plaquettes dans la dysfonction de l'endothélium sinusoïdal hépatique au cours de la maladie stéatosique hépatique associée aux troubles métaboliques
positions.host_institution: I2MC - Institut des Maladies Métaboliques et Cardiovasculaires
positions.research_field: Platelets are the first cells to interact with damaged liver vasculature, yet we know surprisingly little about how they reshape the endothelial environment in disease. This interdisciplinary PhD will combine cutting-edge platelet biology in Toulouse with world-leading expertise in liver endothelial immunology in Birmingham to answer questions neither team can address independently, and uncover how platelet-derived signals drive vascular dysfunction in metabolic liver diseases and carcinogenesis.

positions.title: Rôle et modulation pharmacologique d'un nouveau régulateur de l'adaptation métabolique mitochondriale dans le muscle squelettique au cours des maladies métaboliques et du vieillissement
positions.host_institution: I2MC - Institut des Maladies Métaboliques et Cardiovasculaires
positions.research_field:
The research theme of the PhD project falls within the BEST thematic pillar “Understanding and promoting health and well-being.” (Le domaine de recherche du projet de these s'inscrit dans le pillier thématique BEST “comprendre et promouvoir la santé et le bien-être”). 
More specifically, the research that will be developed during the PhD project lies at the intersection of mitochondrial biology, skeletal muscle physiology, metabolic diseases, and ageing, with a strong focus on translational and therapeutic perspectives. By combining cellular and molecular approaches, including the evaluation of a first-in-class pharmacological compound, with functional analyses of mitochondrial respiration, energy metabolism, muscle differentiation, and exercise-related signaling, the project seeks to identify therapeutically actionable mechanisms and develop novel pharmacological strategies for the prevention and treatment of metabolic and age-related muscle disorders.

positions.research_field: Le projet relève de la recherche translationnelle en santé, à l'interface entre l'ingénierie instrumentale, la chimie analytique et la biologie. Il mobilise le développement et l'automatisation de prototypes, la spectrométrie de masse, la biologie cellulaire, la microbiologie et la pharmacologie, ainsi que l'analyse de données. Ses applications concernent principalement les maladies infectieuses et le sepsis, avec des perspectives d'extension à d'autres pathologies et à d'autres secteurs.
